# New-MftPhysicalSeed.ps1

Creates a one-million-entry, zero-byte MFT seed in a new dynamic VHDX only when explicitly applied in an elevated Windows PowerShell session. Parameters are `-ApprovedRoot` (existing, empty, user-approved local fixed NTFS directory), `-EvidenceParent` (separate existing fixed NTFS directory), `-RunId` (new run GUID), `-VhdxSizeGiB` (64–256; default 96), `-Apply`, and the exact `-ConfirmationToken "CREATE MFT SEED <guid>"`. The displayed plan includes the concrete command, host VHDX path/size, format target/label, 1M workload, and external-monitor limitation. `-WhatIf` and the default no-Apply path stop before filesystem or storage mutations.

The workflow requires administrator context but never self-elevates. Before any storage mutation it resolves and hashes the .NET host executable. After `ShouldProcess` and exact token confirmation, it writes a create-new intent under a separate run-scoped evidence directory, checks 60 GiB of host free space before VHDX creation and immediately before the 1M workload, creates only an absent GUID-named dynamic VHDX, and repeatedly rebinds VHDX file identity, disk unique ID, partition, volume unique ID/GUID, NTFS label, and protected-volume roles before mutation. Run-scoped evidence, seed, workload, build-cache, and publish directories use the atomic `New-MftDirectoryCreateNew` (`CreateDirectoryW`) primitive and fail on `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS`; they are never created with idempotent `Directory.CreateDirectory`. VHDX creation goes through `New-MftVhdxCreateNew`, an injectable create seam whose collision failure is covered offline; this handoff makes no claim that native Hyper-V was run or race-tested. The workload and build caches are isolated under the run evidence root; the seed's own root starts with only the two markers required by FileMutationWorkload. The MFT marker is CreateNew-written after the workload. No failure path deletes, detaches, formats again, or rolls back partial evidence/fixture.

Dependencies: Windows PowerShell 7+, Hyper-V/Storage cmdlets (`New-VHD`, `Get-VHD`, `Mount-VHD`, `Get-Disk`, `Initialize-Disk`, `Get/ New-Partition`, `Get-Volume`, `Format-Volume`), CIM/registry read-only host inventory, .NET file APIs, `dotnet publish`, and `tools/StorageChronicle.FileMutationWorkload`. The script uses Windows CRT-compatible argument quoting for whitespace, embedded quotes, and trailing backslashes; the offline quoting contract is tested in `Test-MftPhysicalSeedContracts.ps1`. The script's static and mocked checks do not execute this workflow. Actual VHDX creation, attach, initialize, partition, format, and 1M workload are deliberately NOT_EXECUTED in this handoff.

Creator-owned intent/marker/completion records are not independent provenance. Completion records `IndependentWriteMonitor.Status=NOT_SUPPLIED` and `AcceptanceEligible=false`. An independently collected process-attributed monitor artifact is still mandatory for the matrix and final acceptance gate. The exact collision and no-Apply contracts are in `Test-MftPhysicalSeedContracts.ps1`; no physical storage operation was executed.
